thread:
ana: Hey support, after pip installing redwood-sdk[grpc,extras] import fails in our CI with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'httpcore._backends'
ana: Repro steps: Python 3.10 venv on ubuntu-latest, workflow runs: `python -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -U pip && .venv/bin/pip install redwood-sdk[extras]`
ana: traceback:
```python
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<frozen importlib._bootstrap>", line 991, in _find_and_load
  File "<frozen importlib._bootstrap>", line 975, in _find_and_load_unlocked
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'httpcore._backends'
```
ben: Hmm, looks like an httpcore/httpx binary/backend mismatch. Can you paste `pip freeze` from the failing runner?
ana: PIP FREEZE from CI:
```text
certifi==2023.5.7
httpcore==0.16.3
httpx==0.23.3
redwood-sdk==0.9.1
typing-extensions==4.5.0
```
ben: Yeah — httpx 0.23.3 expects a different httpcore layout. Suggest upgrading both to a compatible pair, e.g. httpx 0.24.1 + httpcore 0.15.x. On musl/alpine the compiled httpcore wheels can differ which exposes backend import paths.
ana: We also see it only in CI (ubuntu runner using manylinux wheels) and on an alpine-based build where it turns into an SNI/ssl error earlier. Locally on mac it worked.
luis: If you're using poetry, pin the httpx/httpcore versions in pyproject.toml to avoid resolver picking older transitive versions from other deps. Example:
```toml
[tool.poetry.dependencies]
httpx = "^0.24.1"
httpcore = "^0.15.0"
```
ben: Quick workaround: install SDK without deps then install compatible httpx/httpcore manually:
```bash
pip install --no-deps redwood-sdk[grpc]
pip install httpx==0.24.1 httpcore==0.15.0
```
ben: Longer term we'll relax the SDK extras to require a known-good pair and add compatibility notes.
dev-support: Filed an internal follow-up to update docs & add CI note. assigned to @luis — ticket created.
support-bot: ticket #12345 created and linked to thread :ticket: 
ana: Thanks — applying the manual fix in CI now, will report back if it reproduces. :thumbsup:
